To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lower nutritional status is associated with lower cognitive achievement among children aged 8 to 11.
lower height-for-age, weight-for-age, and their corresponding binary measurements (stunting, thinness, underweight) are associated with lower math and reading scores, and lower educational attainment

lower height-for-age and its binary measure were associated with lower math and reading skills, and lower weight-for-age and its corresponding binary measure were associated lower math and reading scores and grade level, with BMI-for-age and its measure marginally associated with grade level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of nutritional status on educational attainment in middle childhood.
the relationship between nutritional outcomes in early childhood and later cognitive outcomes in middle childhood.
the impact of malnutrition on the cognitive achievement of children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relationship between early-life malnutrion and cognitive achievement in children is negative.
nutritional status in early childhood has a long term impact on cognitive development and academic performance.
nutritional status is associated with cognitive achievement, which is associated with educational attainment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
malnutrition is associated with poorer cognitive achievement and lower educational attainment in middle childhood.
nutritional status during childhood is associated with cognitive achievement during childhood.
malnutrition in middle-childhood is associated with lower math and reading scores and lower educational attainment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of early-life malnutrition are long-lasting and that the effects of malnutrition on children's education are not limited to the first 5 years of life.
nutritional interventions that improve children's nutritional status during middle childhood could improve their cognitive development and educational attainment.
early-life malnutrition is associated with lower math and reading scores, and lower educational attainment in middle childhood.
